title: Postgres never updates a row. Here's what it does instead

idea.title: Postgres never updates a row. Here's what it does instead
idea.aha: An UPDATE in Postgres writes a brand-new copy of the row and marks the old one dead, which is how readers never block writers and why the table grows.
idea.pain: You deleted half a table and the disk usage didn't go down, or someone said 'you need to vacuum'.
didntKnow: UPDATE is effectively INSERT a new version + mark the old one expired
Each row version carries the transaction IDs that created and expired it
DELETE doesn't free disk space; VACUUM marks the space reusable, and only VACUUM FULL shrinks the file
Two queries running at the same moment can see different versions of the same row
Transaction IDs are 32-bit, and if they wrap without vacuuming Postgres stops accepting writes
idea.visual: A table page with stacked row versions stamped with xmin/xmax numbers; two reader boxes with snapshot glasses seeing different rows
idea.device: Row version stamps: CREATED BY tx / DELETED BY tx
idea.why: Contrarian title on the most-loved database, with a concrete disk-usage pain
